resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in United States v. Davis, 139 S. Ct. 2319 (2019), holding that § 924(c)'s residual clause is unconstitutionally vague.
issue: Did Johnson and Dimaya render the crime-of-violence residual clause in 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) unconstitutionally vague?

sides.position: Johnson and Dimaya render the § 924(c) residual clause unconstitutionally vague (pre-Davis; the opinion does not name the circuits on this side)
cases: United States v. Davis, 139 S. Ct. 2319 (2019)

sides.position: Johnson and Dimaya do not reach the § 924(c) residual clause (pre-Davis; the opinion does not name the circuits on this side)

quote: Circuit courts split over whether the principles of Johnson and Dimaya rendered § 924(c)'s crime-of-violence residual clause unconstitutional.
cite: In re: Dearnta Thomas, 988 F.3d 783 (4th Cir. 2021)
